messages:
sara: Heads up — we just got 3 customer tickets complaining about huge P99 latency right after the auth-proxy deploy 20m ago. Two of them have traces showing repeated retries. Can someone look?
ops-bot: alert: high_p99_latency service=api-auth env=prod at 2023-05-12T14:02:00Z :rotating_light:
mike: on it. Which dashboards are people looking at? Are we sure this is real and not a panel calc change?
kevin: I see a ~3x jump in the 'api->auth p99 (5m)' panel on the ops-dashboard. But FYI the ingest pipeline changed histogram bucket boundaries last week (le buckets now end at 2000ms instead of 1500ms). That could shift quantile lookups.
sara: customer traces show spikes to ~1.6s and a bunch of 500ms retries. So seems real. Logs attached: `auth-proxy timeout after 800ms`, then client retries.
nina: repro steps (from support ticket): 1) hit /v1/generate with bad header 2) auth-proxy returns 401 with 800ms delay 3) client retries 3x => tail amplification.
mike: okay, hypothesis: auth-proxy change added a blocking call path under certain TTL checks, increasing 99th. We should check request_duration raw histograms and the `.sum`/`.count` to calculate quantiles.
kevin: here's the prometheus query I'm using: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="auth-proxy"}[5m])) by (le))` — but note the dashboard panel uses a rollup exporter that computes p99 from samples instead (approx_quantile rollup) — two different derivations.
eva: @kevin can you post raw bucket counts around the spike? I want to see if there are more counts in the >1s bucket or if it's just redistributed by bucket boundary changes.
kevin: raw buckets, 5m window: le=0.5: 1.2k, le=1.0: 1.25k, le=1.5:1.45k, le=2.0:1.48k, +inf:1.5k. So ~50 requests landed in 1.0-1.5s and ~30 in 1.5-2.0s.
mike: that matches real tail increase. Not just a calc artifact. Also traces show retry amplification.
sara: customer impact = timeouts on upload flow, they see retries and billing spikiness. Support asked for immediate mitigation.
eva: short-term mitigation ideas: 1) rollback proxy change 2) add circuit-breaker to stop retries 3) increase client-side backoff (but can't force clients) 4) configure a temporary routing to a stable auth instance pool.
mike: I'd rather flip a routing fallback to the old auth binary (we have a canary tag) and throttle retries at the proxy level. Rollback only if fallback fails.
kevin: also we should annotate dashboards: panel A uses histogram_quantile over raw buckets, panel B uses rollup approx_quantile. I'll add a note explaining the difference and make both show raw-bucket p99 by default for now.
sara: who will own customer comms? Nina can send interim note: "we're investigating, implemented temporary routing, will update in 30m".
nina: on it.
mike: ops steps I'm taking: 1) enable fallback to old auth binary in prod (5% -> 50% traffic), 2) enable proxy-level retry caps `max_retries=1`, 3) monitor p95/p99 on raw histograms and traces.
kevin: I'll patch dashboards and run a backfill query to compare pre/post bucket behavior: `sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="auth-proxy"}[15m])) by (le)` and compute cumulative.
sara: ETA on rollback/fallback?
mike: fallback enabled in 3m, ramping to 50% now.
ops-bot: deploy: routing-change auth-fallback ramp started by mike at 2023-05-12T14:05:12Z
kevin: after 10m the raw-histogram p99 dropped ~40% on the fallback shard, overall p99 dropped ~20%. Traces show fewer retries.
nina: updated customers: "we've applied a temporary routing change to reduce latency while we investigate root cause. We're monitoring and will follow up".
sara: great. Long-term actions?
mike: 1) revert the problematic auth-proxy change and create a smaller, bench-tested patch 2) add automatic retry amplification protection (e.g., jittered backoff + server-side retry cap) 3) standardize dashboard panels to use raw histogram_quantile for p95/p99 unless explicit approx rollup is needed 4) add an alert that correlates retry-rate with p99 > threshold.
kevin: I'll open a PR to update dashboard and add a short doc about bucket boundary changes affecting quantiles.
eva: I'll work on a proxy feature flag for server-side retry caps so we can toggle without deploy.
sara: thanks all. Putting this thread in incident log. Please add links to PRs and postmortem once done. :white_check_mark:
